applies_why: The judge text does not count a cited verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link; it marks the matter UNDERDETERMINED and says it is answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: 'counts as an unanswered witness' / 'toward a broken link': the judge might be read as merely noting that verses are footing for an analogy, or as counting them as unanswered support for a broken link; the text says UNDERDETERMINED and answered, so it is not the latter.
why: The judge does not count any cited verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link, and it says the challenge is answered, so not counting it obeys K-G4.
